William Saliba (back) and Christos Tzolis (hamstring) remain out. However, Ian Maatsen (ankle) and Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring) remain sidelined, as does long-term absentee Amadou Onana (knee). Fabian Hurzeler isn’t expecting anyone else back, although Mats Wieffer (knee) and Yankuba Minteh (leg) are getting close. The hope for Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) is that he will return in/around the November international break. He’ll still be out for a few weeks, mind. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), Julian Araujo (thigh) and Eli Junior Kroupi (foot) are all reportedly back on the grass, and some could return in the next week or two. Keith Andrews also said that Nathan Collins (calf) and Mikkel Damsgaard (unspecified) could return on Saturday. That leaves Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee), who all remain out. Reece James is set to miss three months of action after undergoing knee surgery. Jamie Gittens (ankle) and Emmanuel Emegha (knock) are also out. The injury to James should mean Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo continue in central midfield, although Romeo Lavia is among those pushing for a recall. However, after last weekend’s 5-1 win over Bournemouth, Xabi Alonso may be tempted to name an unchanged starting XI. Taiwo Awoniyi returns to the squad after completing his three-match ban. Kaine Kesler-Hayden is also available for this game, although match fitness could be an issue. Luke Woolfenden (knee), Aurele Amenda (calf), Josh Eccles (ankle) and Haji Wright (quad) will all miss out. Adam Wharton has played back-to-back 90s but is expected to go again following his rest during the extended international break. Quinten Timber should keep his place alongside him. It sounds like Christian Norgaard will have to settle for a place on the bench again, however. As for the starting XI, Michael Keane will be on standby if any of the defenders miss out. Hugo Larsson (groin) is a doubt, but Alvaro Arbeloa said everyone else is fit. That presumably includes Tom Cairney (knee), who returned to training over the international break, and Antonee Robinson, who missed out last week due to an ankle issue. With Robinson fit, he will likely return to the starting XI at the expense of Ryan Sessegnon. There could be a change on the opposite flank too, with Timothy Castagne in for Kenny Tete. Nobel Mendy has been ruled out for a couple of weeks with a groin problem, with Lucas Herrington his likely replacement on Saturday. Mohamed-Ali Cho (thigh) and Lucas Gourna-Douath (unknown) are also out but could return next week. Elsewhere, Matt Targett is out for two months with an ankle issue, joining Jack Butland (shoulder), Charlie Hughes (groin), Ilyas Ansah (back) and Darko Gyabi (thigh) on the sidelines. The winger will likely come straight back into the starting XI here, potentially with Jack Clarke, leaving Jaden Philogene and Daizen Maeda’s places on the flanks vulnerable. Mateo Joseph (knee) is out for the Whites, however. Leeds have been one of the easiest teams to predict this season, with this the same team that started at Arsenal last time out. Ryan Gravenberch serves a one-match ban after his dismissal for two bookable offences in Gameweek 6. It’s a very tricky Manchester City line-up to predict this week, particularly with a trip to AEK Athens up next on Tuesday. This match also follows demanding clashes with Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain. The central midfield trio subsequently feels like the hardest to predict. Luke Shaw (unspecified), Noussair Mazraoui (back) and Kobbie Mainoo (unspecified), who all missed out in midweek, will be assessed. However, he did say that he could join tomorrow’s training session and that he had a chance to feature, with the extra day of recovery potentially key. If Gibbs-White fails to make it, Callum Hudson-Odoi is the most likely player to come in. Brian Brobbey is in contention to start on Sunday, particularly if Wilson Isidor fails to prove his fitness. The Dutchman returned to the bench for Thursday’s Europa League clash but remained unused.
